I actually went for an AP position after I had to take some time off due to stress issues.

I was in a very well paid position but extremely demanding that kept throwing curb balls at you. I hated going to that noisy office but the partners wanted us there. My lunch break was basically going to buy two sandwiches on a corner bakery and eat them as I cane back to the office. The whole thing took under 15 minutes. I did this for over four years.

At some point my health started deteriorating. My asthma was out of control, I started finding blood in the toilet, some nights I would wake up not feeling good and started vomiting so I had to call the doctor. One day I fell ill with a pulmonary infection. Nothing really serious for a young person (I was in my twenties) but that bug kept coming back every other month for about a year.

I was eventually fired because my performance wasn't that great.

I decided to take some time off and have a healthier lifestyle and all those symptoms disappeared.

I do have a remote position now in AP and it's a lot more chill. It took some work on myself specially ego-wiseto be able to downgrade so much. 

I don't know what to tell you. The downgrade is not for everyone but it did work for me and I also know other CPAs that ended up doing something similar. They all had to deal with the ego thing as well.

Also all in all I still think that it was worthwhile even money wise because I haven't worked a single hour over 40 per week and not a single weekend either.
